title: AI-generated cell-penetrating peptide selected with molecular-dynamics simulations
summary: An RNN generated peptide sequences and molecular-dynamics-based scoring prioritized Pep-MD for synthesis. In cell assays, the authors report less toxicity than TAT and stronger cell permeability under the tested conditions. The paper proposes a membrane-entry mechanism based partly on simulated structures; these cell results do not establish therapeutic efficacy.
ai_technology: Recurrent neural network sequence generator with molecular-dynamics-based selection score
organization: Tokyo Institute of Technology; RIKEN; The University of Tokyo; National Institute for Materials Science

source_review.scope: Primary publisher full PDF, methods/results, publication information and author affiliations.

evidence.tested: The selected synthesized peptide was tested in cell-viability, confocal-imaging and FACS permeability assays against TAT.
evidence.unknown: Cell-based assays and a single comparator; no clinical or therapeutic efficacy evidence; mechanistic interpretation partly depends on modeled structures.
evidence.ai_role: An RNN generated candidate peptides; a simulation-derived score prioritized one sequence for synthesis and experimental cell testing.
